newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks tumble 5.28 pct to near 8-year low.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks tumble 5.28 pct to near 8-year low.

text.p: Thai stocks suffered a heavy battering on Wednesday with concerns over the stumbling economy aggravated by a fresh market attack on the baht.
The composite SET Index lost 5.28 percent shortly after the market reopened in the afternoon. It fell 31.67 points to stay near its eight year low of 568.57 on moderate 3.83 billion baht turnover.
The baht attacks and forced selling of leveraged stocks held by retail investors aggravated the market's slide, they said.
"Stock selling is across the board. Most selling orders are from foreign investors," said a Nava Finance and Securities broker.
Currency dealers dumped the baht for the dollar on Wednesday despite assurances from the Bank of Thailand that it had no plan to change its baht fixing policy.

Concerns over a slowing economy, poor first quarter results, beleaguered property and finance sectors, and uncertainty over the scope of the government's efforts to improve the situation have all been blamed for the market's recent falls.
